strategy.reason: Use one full-video phase index, then spend separate requests on narrow comparison and recurrence questions.

runs.role: Interval 2 versus Interval 3 telemetry-selected window comparison

candidateInsights.title: Interval 3 started unevenly, then produced the biggest build
candidateInsights.telemetryContext: Concept2 shows Interval 3 rising from about 139 W and 26.5 spm in its first minute to about 211 W and 30.5 spm in its final minute.
candidateInsights.directObservation: Pegasus described the opening strokes as slower and less fluid than the other interval starts.
candidateInsights.reviewNote: Use the telemetry-backed build and the directly visible opening description. Do not claim an exact number of strokes before the rhythm became steady.

candidateInsights.title: The strongest interval looked mechanically similar
candidateInsights.telemetryContext: Work 2 averaged about 161 W; Work 4 averaged about 179 W.
candidateInsights.directObservation: Pegasus did not find a reliable visible mechanical difference between equivalent opening, middle, and finishing windows.
candidateInsights.reviewNote: Represent as unresolved visual evidence, not proof that mechanics were identical.

candidateInsights.title: Hydration behavior recurred during recovery
candidateInsights.directObservation: Pegasus found visible hydration events around 11:08 and 25:17 and reported different immediate post-event behavior.
candidateInsights.reviewNote: The athlete confirmed both water breaks. Useful synchronization evidence; probably not a primary coaching insight.

candidateInsights.title: Similar-looking strokes produced very different output
candidateInsights.telemetryContext: Interval 2 candidate window averaged about 157 W at 29.8 spm; Interval 3 candidate window averaged about 215 W at 30.4 spm.
candidateInsights.directObservation: Pegasus reported no reliable visible difference across recovery duration, hands-away timing, body preparation, sequencing, reach, stroke length, or rhythm.
candidateInsights.reviewNote: Represent the visual explanation as unresolved. The telemetry difference is authoritative.

rejectedClaims.claim: Core engagement lags behind leg drive.
rejectedClaims.reason: Core engagement cannot be directly established from the fixed frontal video.

rejectedClaims.claim: The video shows identical mechanics between Work 2 and Work 4.
rejectedClaims.reason: Absence of a detected difference should be recorded as unresolved, not identity.

rejectedClaims.claim: Interval 3 took exactly four strokes to settle.
rejectedClaims.reason: The provider did not define a measurable threshold for 'settled'; preserve only the broader directly visible description.
